newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Another bomb hits Algerian capital.
newsitem.headline: Another bomb hits Algerian capital.

text.p: A bomb exploded in the Algerian capital early on Monday, only hours after two others on buses had killed up to 11 people and wounded 77 in the countdown to a parliamentary election on Thursday.
A resident said the latest blast was caused by a bomb in Bab El-Oued, a crowded, working class, inner city area. No details were immediately available and there was no official statement.
Foreign journalists, in Algiers to cover the election meant to end over five years of violence the authorities blame on Moslem fundamentalists, heard the huge blast at about 8.30 a.m. (0730 GMT).
On Sunday, two bombs exploded on buses in the heart of Algiers. The official death toll was seven, with 77 wounded. Newspapers on Monday quoted medical sources as saying 11 had died.

Bombs have killed hundreds of people and wounded thousands in the conflict between Moslem rebels and security forces, and early this year Algiers city authorities brought in draconian parking measures to try to thwart car bombs.

More than 200,000 troops and security forces are expected to be deployed nationwide for Thursday's parliamentary election to protect the nearly 18 million registered voters. But residents said there were few signs so far of extra security in the capital.

Algeria has been without a parliament since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding first round lead. Violence erupted shortly afterwards and about 60,000 people have been killed.
